items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: The transcript identifies Monk Rowe as the [INTERVIEWER] conducting the interview with Ray Conniff. No personal or professional relationship beyond the interviewer-interviewee dynamic is described.

ctx.x: His distinctive blend of big band, orchestral and vocal scoring captured the ears of American listeners in the late 1950s and became a familiar sound on radio and home stereos. He started as a trombonist and arranger in the active years of swing, writing for Bunny Berigan, Artie Shaw, Benny Goodman and other big band leaders. His association with Mitch Miller at Columbia Records led to his first records under his own name, and he now places on the top ten all-time album sellers. His six decade career in music is…
Ray currently lives in Los Angeles, and was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 14, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

We are filming in San Diego for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. And I am honored to have Mr. Ray Conniff with me — trombonist and arranger and composer. And I want to tell you that when I grew up, in the 50s, I lived outside Rochester, New York, and it was kind of a typical suburban home, and in my house, my parents played Glenn Miller and a little Basie, and a lot of Ray Conniff.
